fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Moses never says the millstones belong to the town. His reason is that taking them "…would be taking one’s livelihood as security." The stones are tied to how a man makes his living, and a lender who grabs them leaves him with nothing to work with.

Yes, baker. She says, "My husband’s brother refuses to preserve his brother’s name in Israel. He is not willing to perform the duty of a brother-in-law for me." Notice she isn't dragging him off to a fight. She walks to the city gate and lays it out in front of the elders (Deuteronomy 25:7). And the elders don't just rule on the spot. They summon him and talk with him first (Deuteronomy 25:8).

Fair is a good word, baker, but Moses never brings up a tithe here. He ties honest weights and measures to this: "…so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you." Picture a cookie box with a thumb on the scale. Moses doesn't say the priests are watching it. He says the whole land is at stake.
